text.title: C# Clean Architecture + CQRS Core Rules
text.summary: 17 testable rules grounding the Clean Architecture + CQRS pattern for .NET 8/9 — layering, aggregate design, the CQRS message contract, the MediatR pipeline, and the library-licensing constraints that decide the bus. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: Project references point inward only: API → Application → Domain ← Infrastructure. Domain MUST have zero outward references — no `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`, no `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*`, no external SDK of any kind. Application MUST NOT reference Infrastructure, `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`, or `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*`.
rule.rationale: Inward dependency direction keeps Domain stable; any Application-on-Infrastructure reference collapses the layering and re-introduces a big-ball-of-mud.

rule.statement: Business behaviour MUST live on Domain entity methods (e.g. `user.Activate()`). Application handlers orchestrate the call but MUST NOT host the rule (no `if (user.IsActive) throw` in a handler).
rule.rationale: Behaviour in handlers leaves entities as property bags; invariants leak and the layering's value evaporates.

rule.statement: Each use-case MUST live in `Application/Features/<Feature>/<UseCase>/` with a single Command/Query, a single Handler, an optional Validator, and an optional Response — one folder, one use-case.
rule.rationale: One-per-folder makes the agent surface area tiny; mixed folders multiply the cognitive load per change.

rule.statement: Input validation MUST live in a FluentValidation `AbstractValidator<T>` on the Command/Query DTO, registered via `AddValidatorsFromAssembly(...)` and run by a MediatR validation pipeline behaviour BEFORE the handler; the resulting `ValidationException` maps to a 400 `ProblemDetails`. Domain invariants stay in entity factories. DataAnnotation attributes on DTOs and `if (req.Foo == null) throw` inside handlers are forbidden.
rule.rationale: Three validation surfaces (annotations + validator + entity) drift; a single FluentValidation site keeps the contract testable and reusable. Running it in the pipeline rather than the handler is what makes the 400 shape uniform across every use-case.

rule.statement: Domain events that touch other aggregates MUST be dispatched via the Outbox pattern (e.g. MassTransit Outbox) — never inline inside the same `SaveChangesAsync` transaction.
rule.rationale: Inline cross-aggregate handlers roll back the outer transaction on a downstream failure; outbox makes the dispatch atomic with the write and retried independently.

rule.statement: MediatR MUST be reserved for use-cases with cross-cutting needs (validation pipeline, auth pipeline, transaction pipeline, logging). Trivial reads (`GET /health`, simple lookups) MUST NOT be wrapped in Commands/Queries.
rule.rationale: Every dispatch pays handler resolution + pipeline overhead; wrapping `/health` adds latency for no benefit. On a solo codebase the pipeline overhead exceeds its benefit for most use-cases.

rule.statement: Every command/query is a `record` implementing `IRequest<TResponse>` with exactly one `IRequestHandler<TRequest, TResponse>` in `Application/`, and the handler's `Handle` MUST accept a `CancellationToken`. Generic `IService` classes that mix several operations are forbidden, and so are the `Command`/`Handler`/`Validator`/`Response` suffixes being dropped.

rationale.source: MediatR docs + Jimmy Bogard CQRS posts

rule.rationale: One handler per message preserves the read/write separation and makes pipeline behaviours attachable in one place. Reading the handler signature tells an agent the full input/output schema; a mixed `Service` class hides it. A `Handle` overload without a token is the reliable signature that the code was generated against MediatR v9.

rule.statement: Aggregates and entities MUST have no public setters (only `private set` plus a factory or constructor). State changes go through intention-revealing methods that enforce invariants — `order.Ship(carrier, when)`, never `order.Status = "shipped"`. Domain events are raised inside the aggregate method.
rule.rationale: Public setters let a caller bypass every invariant, so the aggregate cannot enforce a rule consistently. Code-gen agents emit `{ get; set; }` because that is the ASP.NET Core training-data norm, which is exactly why this needs a lint rather than a convention.

rule.statement: The API layer MUST NOT return Domain entities. Responses are `record` DTOs defined in `Application/` (or `Web/Contracts/`); entities never appear in a controller signature, a MediatR response, or a Swagger schema. One DTO per query — `GetUsersListItemDto` and `GetUserDetailDto` stay two types even at 80% overlap.
rule.rationale: Returning an entity couples the persistence shape to the public contract: adding a column or a navigation breaks every client, and Swagger starts advertising `Discriminator` and `RowVersion`. A shared DTO causes over-projection and turns "I added a field" into five broken endpoints.

rule.statement: `IQueryable<T>` MUST NOT cross out of the Application layer. Paging and projection happen inside the handler; the handler returns materialized DTOs.
rule.rationale: An agent asked for "flexibility" returns `IQueryable` and the query then executes in the API layer, after the scope that owned the context — or with LINQ the handler never sanctioned.

rule.statement: Application declares `IApplicationDbContext`; Infrastructure owns the concrete `ApplicationDbContext`. Handlers MUST NOT inject `DbContext` directly, and MUST NOT read `HttpContext` or `IHttpContextAccessor` — handlers are transport-agnostic.
rule.rationale: Injecting DbContext into a handler puts EF in the Application layer through the back door without a csproj reference to catch it. A handler that reads HttpContext cannot be dispatched from a worker, a test, or a queue consumer.

rule.statement: `IPipelineBehavior<,>` registrations are ordered explicitly and in one place: Logging → Validation → Authorization → UnitOfWork → Caching → Handler. The order is asserted by a test, not assumed from DI registration order.
rule.rationale: Pipeline order follows DI registration order, so a mis-registration silently disables validation instead of failing — a validator registered after the handler never runs and nothing in the build says so.

rule.statement: Each layer exposes one `AddApplication()` / `AddInfrastructure()` extension method; `Program.cs` is the only composition root and calls nothing else.
rule.rationale: A single composition root keeps agent-driven service registration deterministic and keeps `Program.cs` short enough that a reviewer can see the whole DI graph.

rule.statement: Pin the mediator and mapper major versions in `Directory.Packages.props` and name the library explicitly in every prompt. Prefer source-generated, free alternatives — `Mediator` over MediatR, Mapperly over AutoMapper — in any commercial product: MediatR v12+ and AutoMapper v10+ require a paid license above $1M revenue.
rule.rationale: The license change is a business constraint that becomes a rewrite if discovered after adoption. Separately, MediatR / Mediator / Wolverine have incompatible APIs, and an unnamed library is how an agent emits v9 code against a v12 project.

rule.statement: Use `DomainException` only for invariant violations. Expected failures ("user not found", "already shipped") return a `Result`/`ErrorOr` value, mapped to the HTTP status in the API layer.
rule.rationale: Exceptions for expected outcomes turn every handler into a try/catch cargo cult and hide the real failure paths from the signature.

rule.statement: Domain events are added on the aggregate (`user.AddDomainEvent(...)`) inside the method that caused them, published from the `SaveChangesAsync` override or an outbox relay, and CLEARED after publish.
rule.rationale: Two failures are both common: adding the event and never overriding SaveChangesAsync to publish it, and publishing without clearing, which re-fires every event on the next save.

rule.statement: Each feature carries at least one integration test using `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` + a Testcontainers database, in addition to the handler unit test. Mocking `IMediator.Send(...)` and asserting a call count does not satisfy this rule.
rule.rationale: A stubbed bus asserts that the controller called something; it cannot see handler resolution failures or a pipeline behaviour registered in the wrong order, which are the two bugs this architecture actually produces.
